records.title: Leaving mdx out of pageExtensions broke only the dev server
records.summary: The production build passed while every lesson page in dev failed with an error about React internals.
records.problem: A Next.js dev server fails on MDX pages with a React internals error while the production build passes.
records.approach: Set pageExtensions to only ts and tsx so MDX files outside app/ would not become routes; found the dev build compiled .mdx against userland React because Next's alias condition is built from pageExtensions. Adding mdx to pageExtensions held.
records.conditions: Next.js App Router site with MDX content under content/ outside app/, pageExtensions set in next.config.ts.
records.evidence: Fix in next.config.ts (pageExtensions: ["ts", "tsx", "mdx"]); alias rules in node_modules/next/dist/build/create-compiler-aliases.js
records.implication: When a change touches next.config.ts, open one page of each kind in the dev server before calling it done.
records.text: Lessons live under content/ , outside app/ , so pageExtensions was set to "ts", "tsx" to keep MDX files from becoming routes by accident. next build passed and rendered every page. next dev failed on every lesson with Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'recentlyCreatedOwnerStacks' , an error from React's development JSX runtime that says nothing about MDX or configuration. The compiled lesson chunk imported node_modules/react/jsx-dev-runtime.js , the userland React, while the page around it ran on the React that Next vendors. Next aliases react/jsx-runtime to its own copy only for files that match its code condition, and that condition is built from pageExtensions . An .mdx file outside the list was compiled but never aliased. Production uses the plain JSX runtime, which does not touch the field, so only development broke. Evidence: .next/server/_rsc_content_lessons_..._index_mdx.js importing rsc /./node_modules/react/jsx-runtime.js ; the alias rules in node_modules/next/dist/build/create-compiler-aliases.js ; the fix in next.config.ts pageExtensions: "ts", "tsx", "mdx" . Implications: a green next build does not show that next dev works. When a change touches next.config.ts , open one page of each kind in the dev server before calling it done. An error from deep inside React that mentions internals usually means two copies of React met, so check which react each chunk imports before reading the stack.

records.title: The coordinator deleted the folder a subagent was converting
records.summary: While four subagents converted lessons, the coordinator committed the deletion of the folder one of them was reading from.
records.problem: A coordinator agent changed or deleted files that a running subagent was told to read.
records.approach: Four subagents converted lessons in parallel while the coordinator ran git rm -r on the folder they read from. One subagent recovered the sources from the earlier commit with git archive and finished.
records.conditions: Four parallel subagents converting namaq lessons to MDX from one live checkout while the coordinator edited the same checkout.
records.evidence: namaq commit 773a035d removing docs/lessons/; subagent report of reading from git archive 607669f6
records.implication: Hand a subagent a snapshot (a commit hash or a scratchpad copy), and do not delete or move anything a running subagent was told to read.
records.text: Four subagents converted namaq's lessons to MDX in parallel, each told to read the old HTML from namaq's docs/lessons/ . While they ran, the coordinator moved on to the namaq half of the move and ran git rm -r docs/lessons in the same checkout. One subagent found its sources gone halfway through lesson 0001. It recovered them from the commit before the deletion with git archive and finished, and the text-parity check later showed nothing lost. A less careful agent would have reported "files not found" or, worse, converted from memory. Evidence: namaq commit 773a035d removing docs/lessons/ , made while the text-to-evidence conversion was still running; that subagent's report of reading from git archive 607669f6 . Implications: a delegated task's inputs are frozen until it reports back. Hand a subagent a snapshot a commit hash, or a copy in the scratchpad , not a live path in a checkout someone else is editing, and do not delete or move anything a running subagent was told to read.

records.title: Date.parse accepted the thirtieth of February
records.summary: A date check built on Date.parse let 2026-02-30 through, and its test could not notice because it only tried a month that does not exist.
records.problem: Validating that a YYYY-MM-DD string is a real calendar date in JavaScript.
records.approach: Checked the pattern and that Date.parse did not return NaN; review showed V8 rolls 2026-02-30 over to March 2, so the check now round-trips the date through toISOString and compares.
records.conditions: Node 22 and Bun on V8/JavaScriptCore; dates written as plain YYYY-MM-DD strings in record metadata.
records.evidence: distillate PR #4, first review cycle; lib/records.ts checkRecord
records.implication: Test a date validator with a day that overflows its month (2026-02-30, 2026-04-31), not only with an impossible month.
records.text: The record schema requires a date in YYYY-MM-DD form. The first check matched the pattern and called Date.parse , treating NaN as invalid. The test for "not a real calendar date" used 2026-13-45 , which every parser rejects, so it passed. The reviewer tried 2026-02-30 . Date.parse returned a timestamp for March 2: the engine rolls an overflowing day into the next month instead of refusing it. Any record could have claimed a day that never happened. The fix parses the string as UTC midnight and requires toISOString .slice 0, 10 to give back the same string. A rolled-over date comes back different and fails. Evidence: lib/records.ts checkRecord , and the tests for 2026-02-30 and 2026-04-31 in lib/records.test.ts. Implications: a date check is only as good as the cases it is shown to reject. Include a day that overflows its month, since that is the case lenient parsers accept.

records.title: The fix for a stale search box wiped what the reader was typing
records.summary: Resyncing a search box from the URL treated the URL's own lag as an outside change and reset the box mid-typing.
records.problem: Keeping a text input that writes to the URL in step with the URL when the URL also changes from outside, such as back navigation or a link.
records.approach: First reset the box whenever the URL's q differed from the last value written, which wiped text while router.replace lagged behind typing; now the component remembers the values it wrote and resets only for a value it never wrote.
records.conditions: Next.js 15 App Router client component using useSearchParams and router.replace, where the URL updates after the input's own state.
records.evidence: distillate PR #5; components/records/RecordSearch.tsx and its tests
records.implication: A component that writes to the URL must tell its own pending writes apart from outside navigation; test it with a URL that arrives one keystroke behind.
records.text: The records search box keeps its text in React state and writes it to the URL as q . Review found that the box kept "highlight" after the reader followed a link to /records , because the state was read from the URL only on mount. The first fix compared the URL's q on every render with the last value the component had written, and reset the box when they differed. Writing the regression test showed what that did while typing: router.replace lands after the input's own re-render, so for a moment the URL still holds the previous text, which differs from what was just written, and the box was reset to it. A fast typist would have watched letters vanish. The fix that held keeps a short list of values the component wrote. When the URL's q changes to one of them, it is the component's own write arriving late and is ignored. Any other value came from outside, so the box takes it. The check only reads the list and clears it, so running it twice in one render changes nothing. Evidence: components/records/RecordSearch.tsx; the tests "keeps the latest typed text when the URL arrives one keystroke behind" and "clears the search box when the URL loses its query after mount" in components/records/RecordSearch.test.tsx. Implications: two-way sync between an input and the URL needs to know which changes are its own. Test it with the URL lagging, not only with the URL updating at once.

records.title: A mock router too fast to show the race it was meant to catch
records.summary: A regression test for a URL race passed on the broken code, because the mocked router updated the URL instantly.
records.problem: A test of a timing bug passes on the code it is meant to catch, because the test double removes the timing.
records.approach: Ran the new test against the code before the fix, saw it pass, and made the mocked router.replace skip the URL update for the typing step so the URL lags as in the browser; the test then failed on the old code and passed on the fix.
records.conditions: Vitest with jsdom, next/navigation mocked so that router.replace sets the search string synchronously.
records.evidence: distillate PR #5; the test "keeps the typed text when a filter changes before the URL catches up"
records.implication: Run every regression test against the code before the fix and watch it fail; when a race is involved, make the double reproduce the delay.
records.text: Review reported that changing a filter right after typing could drop the typed text from the URL. The test written for it typed, changed a filter, and checked the URL. It passed on the fixed code, and it also passed on the old code. The mock for next/navigation updated the search string inside router.replace , so the next render already saw the new URL. In the browser, replace lands later, which is the whole bug. The mock had removed the delay the test was about. Making the mocked replace skip the update for the typing step put the delay back. The test then failed on the old code, passed on the fix, and in passing exposed a second bug in the first fix see the record that builds on this one . Evidence: components/records/RecordSearch.test.tsx, where the test calls nav.replace.mockImplementationOnce = {} before typing. Implications: a test that has not been seen to fail on the old code has not been shown to test anything. For timing bugs, the double has to keep the timing.

records.title: A trailing slash in .gitignore let a node_modules symlink into the commit
records.summary: node_modules/ in .gitignore matches only directories, so a worktree's node_modules symlink was committed.
records.problem: A symlinked node_modules in a git worktree is committed even though .gitignore lists node_modules/.
records.approach: Spotted the symlink in the staged files after commit, removed it from the index and changed the ignore rule to node_modules without the slash, which matches files and symlinks too.
records.conditions: Git worktree whose node_modules is a symlink to the main checkout's, staged with git add -A.
records.evidence: distillate PR #4; .gitignore
records.implication: Ignore node_modules without a trailing slash in repositories whose worktrees symlink it, and read git status before committing with git add -A.
records.text: Worktrees here share the main checkout's packages through a symlink: each worktree's node_modules points at the main checkout's. The repository ignored node_modules/ . In git's ignore syntax a trailing slash means "directories only", and a symlink is a file, so git add -A staged it. The commit summary listed A node_modules . The fix was git rm --cached node_modules and an ignore rule without the slash, which matches a file, a symlink or a directory of that name. Evidence: .gitignore. Implications: where worktrees symlink shared folders, ignore them without the trailing slash, and look at what git add -A staged before committing.

records.title: Arabic inside English prose has no element to style, so the font itself had to be larger
records.summary: Inline Arabic in MDX paragraphs carries no markup, so setting it larger than the English needed size-adjust on a self-hosted Arabic face.
records.problem: Setting Arabic words larger than the English around them when they sit inline in prose with no element, class or lang attribute to target.
records.approach: Put the Arabic face after the English serif in one font stack so Arabic glyphs fall back to it, and self-hosted its Arabic subset through next/font/local with a size-adjust declaration, since next/font/google takes no declarations.
records.conditions: Next.js 15 next/font; MDX lessons may not carry class, className or style; Amiri's Arabic subset from Google Fonts; inline Arabic in lessons such as text-to-evidence 0006.
records.evidence: app/fonts.ts (amiri, size-adjust 140%); app/globals.css (--font-serif)
records.implication: Size a script that appears inline by the font's size-adjust, not by markup; a value near 122% still read smaller than the English, 140% matched the intent.
records.text: The restyle asked for Arabic set larger than English. Blocks were easy: ArabicQuote is a component and takes its own size. Most Arabic in the lessons is inline, though, inside an English sentence, such as the lemmas «كلا، إن، لا، ما» in lesson 6. Lessons may not carry class , className or style , and the words carry no lang , so there is no element to give a size. The size went into the font instead. The serif stack lists EB Garamond first and Amiri second, so every Arabic glyph falls back to Amiri. A size-adjust declaration on Amiri's @font-face scales only those glyphs. next/font/google has no option for declarations, so Amiri's Arabic subset is self-hosted under app/fonts/ with its licence and loaded through next/font/local , which does. The first value, 122%, still read smaller than the English beside it in a screenshot; 140% matched. Evidence: app/fonts.ts and the --font-serif token in app/globals.css. Implications: when one script appears inline in another's prose and the content cannot carry markup, scale it with the face's size-adjust and check the result in a screenshot rather than by the number.

records.title: A quiz test that asserted colour class names pinned the palette
records.summary: Moving the quiz's right and wrong colours to theme tokens failed a test that matched /green/ and /red/ in the class string.
records.problem: A component test asserts styling class names, so a restyle that keeps the behaviour fails the test.
records.approach: Replaced the quiz's green and red utilities with theme tokens, saw Quiz.test.tsx fail on toMatch(/green/), and went back to green and red utilities with dark variants, since the owner asked to keep tests as they are.
records.conditions: Vitest with jsdom; components/mdx/Quiz.test.tsx checks className against /green/ and /red/; restyle to theme tokens in app/globals.css.
records.evidence: components/mdx/Quiz.test.tsx (marks the correct option green and the clicked wrong option red); components/mdx/Quiz.tsx
records.implication: Assert what the reader is told (the ✓ and ✗ marks and their screen-reader text), not class names; changing Quiz.test.tsx that way would let the quiz use the theme tokens.
records.text: The restyle moved every colour to theme tokens. The quiz's right and wrong answers became border-solved and border-failed , and the suite failed: expected 'w-full rounded-sm border … border-solved text-solved' to match /green/ . The test was named for what the reader sees "marks the correct option green" but checked the class string. Nothing the reader would notice had changed. The owner had asked to keep tests as they were, so the quiz went back to Tailwind's green and red utilities with dark variants, and the two quiz colours stay outside the token set. Evidence: components/mdx/Quiz.test.tsx and components/mdx/Quiz.tsx. Implications: a test of a visual state should assert the state the reader is given, here the ✓ and ✗ marks and the screen-reader text the component already renders. Rewriting this test that way is the follow-up that lets the quiz take the palette.

records.title: A test against the shared link list misses a menu that keeps its own
records.summary: A test against the shared link list missed a menu that keeps its own array of hrefs.
records.problem: A test that compares against a shared list misses a second copy of that list kept in a component.
records.approach: A new page was in getAllNavLinks but not in the desktop menu's own QURAN_SUBMENU_HREFS; adding it and a test looping over every /quran/ link in the shared list expecting each in the submenu held.
records.conditions: Next.js app navbar with the shared list in src/lib/siteLinks.ts and a separate hrefs array in src/components/common/NavBar.tsx.
records.evidence: namaq PR #398 diff, fixed in #399; QURAN_SUBMENU_HREFS in src/components/common/NavBar.tsx
records.implication: When adding a page, grep a sibling page's href and touch every list that names pages, and derive test expectations from the shared list.
records.text: /quran/branches shipped in 398 with a card on /quran and an entry in getAllNavLinks , and the owner could not find it in the navbar. The desktop Quran menu does not read that list. It keeps its own array of hrefs, QURAN_SUBMENU_HREFS in src/components/common/NavBar.tsx , and nothing tied the two together. The hub test compares the cards against getAllNavLinks , so it passed, and the NavBar test named each page by hand, so it passed too. Both checks were green, and neither one could see the gap. Evidence: 398's diff added the page to src/lib/siteLinks.ts and QuranHub.tsx only. 399 adds it to QURAN_SUBMENU_HREFS , and its test loops over every /quran/ link in getAllNavLinks and expects each one in the desktop submenu. The test fails with the fix removed. Implications: when a page is added, look for every list that names pages, not only the one a test compares against: grep for a sibling page's href here /quran/words and touch every hit. A test that names its expected values by hand only catches the pages someone thought of. A test that derives them from the shared list catches the next page too.

records.title: Fixing the highlight the owner pointed at broke the one next to it
records.summary: Four highlight rules, each checked only on the ayah named in the message, each moved highlights nobody looked at.
records.problem: A rule that runs over a whole text was fixed and checked only on the example the owner named, and it moved results nobody looked at.
records.approach: Four highlight rules each broke a neighbouring ayah; a before/after diff of every mark over all 5,082 matches led to pairing the ayat of equal windows in order, which changed 93 matches and held.
records.conditions: The similar-ayat view colours a word amber when the other side has it letter for letter; 5,082 matches in similar.json.
records.evidence: Commits on claude/similar-ayat from "ignore a leading wa or fa" to "link each similar-ayat highlight to its partner"; src/lib/quran/similar.ts (marks, paired)
records.implication: Diff a changed data file against the previous one and read a sample, and add stated invariants to src/lib/quran/similar.test.ts as checks over every pair.
records.text: The similar-ayat view colours a word amber when the other side has it letter for letter. The owner asked why the لا of الحاقة ٣٩ وما لا تبصرون was amber: it matched the فلا of an oath in الواقعة ٧٥. The fix stopped colouring a particle that stands alone. It was checked against that one ayah, which came out right, and shipped. The owner's next message: the إنه that opens both الواقعة ٧٧ and الحاقة ٤٠ had lost its colour. Four highlight rules went in that way in under an hour, each checked only on the ayah named in the message, and each moved highlights nobody looked at. The rule that finally held came from a before/after diff of every mark in all 5,082 matches. The diff showed that pairing the ayat of two equal windows in order ٧٥↔٣٨، ٧٦↔٣٩، ٧٧↔٤٠ changed 93 matches, against hundreds for the earlier rules, and the changed rows could be read one by one. Evidence: the commits on claude/similar-ayat from "ignore a leading wa or fa" to "link each similar-ayat highlight to its partner", and src/lib/quran/similar.ts marks and paired . Implications: a rule that runs over the whole text has to be judged over the whole text. Before reporting a change to similar.json , diff its marks against the previous file and read a sample of what changed. Every rule that can be stated as an invariant belongs in src/lib/quran/similar.test.ts as a check over every pair, as "no mark lacks a partner" now is. The example the owner named only shows that the rule handles one case.

records.title: The unresolved-name count includes battles, and no edit can clear them
records.summary: The unresolved-name count includes battles, which no edit can clear because they are events, not people.
records.problem: A count of unresolved items includes entries that the resolution mechanism can never clear, so the number cannot be driven to zero.
records.approach: Tried to resolve 16 unresolved names; none moved, and 5 were battles, objects of PARTICIPATED_IN, which an agent identification cannot cover. The record proposes reporting event mentions apart from people.
records.conditions: coverageOf counts every mention without a live identification, and an identification names an agent; al-Zubayr's entry had 16 unresolved names.
records.evidence: src/lib/model/coverage.ts (unresolved filter); data/works/siyar-alam-al-nubala/summary.md
records.implication: Decide how a mention points at an event, or report event mentions apart from people, before treating the count as work to finish.
records.text: Sixteen names were unresolved in al-Zubayr's entry, and the task was to resolve them. None moved, and five of them are not people at all: بَدْرٍ twice , اليَرْمُوْكِ , الخَنْدَقِ and فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ are the objects of PARTICIPATED_IN . coverageOf counts every mention without a live identification, and an identification names an agent, so an event mention can never leave the count. Evidence: src/lib/model/coverage.ts the unresolved filter , and the "Unresolved names, dated sentences and office" section of data/works/siyar-alam-al-nubala/summary.md . Implications: the number "16 unresolved names" mixes people owed an identification with events that have no mechanism for one. Decide how a mention points at an event, or report event mentions apart from people, before anyone treats the count as work to finish.

records.title: A fix in the code does not fix the rows built before it
records.summary: A fix in the code did not change the stored rows built before it, and the page kept serving them.
records.problem: A code fix has no effect on a page because it reads stored rows built by the old code.
records.approach: After fixing sceneLines, the page still showed the repeat; the page reads model_units first. Re-running the projection from the checkout holding the change fixed it, after a first run from the main checkout rebuilt the old output.
records.conditions: Page reads model_units and falls back to files only when the row is missing; the projection command was run against the preview environment.
records.evidence: npm run model:project -- --units --root src/lib/model/fixtures/jibril --apply --env preview; src/lib/model/hadithView.ts
records.implication: After changing code that builds a stored view, run the projection from the checkout that holds the change and say so in the PR; consider storing a builder version in each row.
records.text: Scene 1 of both hadith began by repeating the last narrator of the isnad: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، right under a bubble already labelled أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ . The cause was one line in sceneLines src/lib/model/hadithView.ts that started the scene at the last isnad link instead of after it. The fix was small, the new test passed, and the page on localhost still showed the repeat. The page reads model_units first and only falls back to the files when the row is missing, so it was faithfully serving a view built before the fix. The owner then ran the projection to rebuild the rows. Nothing changed. That command ran in the main checkout, which did not have the branch, so it rebuilt the rows from the old code with great care. Running the same command from the worktree finished the job. Evidence: the same text on screen after the fix, then the correct text after the second projection npm run model:project -- --units --root src/lib/model/fixtures/jibril --apply --env preview , run from the checkout that holds the change . The unit test never saw the problem, because hadithView builds from the files and the page does not. Implications: a green test says the builder is right, not that the page is. Any change to the code that builds a stored view needs a projection run from the checkout that holds the change, and the PR should say so. An improvement axis: store a builder version or a hash in each model_units row, and let the page rebuild from the files when it does not match, so a stale row cannot outlive the code that made it. Same family as 0007-a-page-that-reads-the-repo-at-request-time /records/namaq/0007-a-page-that-reads-the-repo-at-request-time .

records.title: A subagent said green while lint and tsc were red
records.summary: A subagent's "all passing" covered the command it ran while lint and tsc were red.
records.problem: A subagent reports its tests pass while lint and the type checker fail and the tests assert little.
records.approach: The subagent reported 20 tests passing; running lint, tsc and the suite revealed errors, forbidden comments and weak assertions, and the tests were rewritten. A separate reviewer's partial notes found four weak spots.
records.conditions: Small subagent wrote tests for the isnad diagram; the reviewer subagent died on an API error but left partial notes; AGENTS.md forbids explanatory comments.
records.evidence: src/lib/model/isnadGraph.test.ts and src/components/hadith/HadithUnit.test.tsx rewrites
records.implication: Run lint, tsc and the whole suite yourself and read what each test asserts; the test writer and reviewer should be different agents.
records.text: A small subagent wrote the tests for the isnad diagram and reported "20 tests, all passing, no problems found." They did pass. npm run lint failed on an unused variable, npx tsc --noEmit failed on a type error in one test, and the files were full of explanatory comments that AGENTS.md forbids. A test titled "hadith with no scenes still shows the diagram and matn" rendered bukhari-jibril , which has scenes. It was a very thorough test of a different question. The reviewer subagent then died partway through on an API error, but its partial notes still found four weak spots, including that one: three tests only checked that some h3 existed, and the "correct order" test never checked the order. Evidence: lint and tsc output after the subagent's report, and the rewritten tests in src/lib/model/isnadGraph.test.ts and src/components/hadith/HadithUnit.test.tsx . Implications: a subagent's "passing" covers the command it ran and nothing else. Run lint, tsc and the whole suite yourself, and read what each test asserts, since a name is a claim and not a check. This is why AGENTS.md now asks for a review before a PR, and why a test writer and a reviewer should not be the same agent. A reviewer that crashes still leaves its partial findings, so read them before retrying.

records.title: With physics on, two chains became one
records.summary: A force engine with physics on stacked two chains into one; a layout function drew the known shape.
records.problem: A force-directed graph layout overlaps nodes when drawing a known, fixed shape such as a diamond of two chains.
records.approach: Tried the existing engine with dagMode="td", where wide nodes landed on the same x; a small rank-and-spread function drawing static SVG drew the diamond correctly every time.
records.conditions: Nodes 200 px wide; the force simulation treats nodes as points; isnad of one hadith (Bukhari one chain, Muslim two chains meeting at Yahya).
records.evidence: namaq PR #344, renderings on muslim-jibril before the force version was removed
records.implication: Use a layout function to draw a known shape and the force engine for questions about a network; the two views can coexist.
records.text: The isnad diagram needed to draw one chain Bukhari's and a diamond Muslim's two chains meeting at Yahya . The graph engine already in the app has a dagMode , so it was tried first. With dagMode="td" the library fixes each node's level and leaves the other axis to the force simulation. The simulation treats a node as a point, and the nodes here are 200 pixels wide. Both Muslim branches landed on the same x and stacked on top of each other, so the diamond became one very confident column. Adding a strong repulsion force made it a diagonal, and the canvas zoomed in on the wreckage. A small function that gives each node a rank from the collector, and spreads each rank sideways, drew the diamond correctly every time as static SVG. It also kept the Arabic text selectable and let a node be a real link. Evidence: both renderings on muslim-jibril before the force version was removed PR 344 . The owner then asked for the collector to be the first node, which meant changing one line: rank from the collector instead of from the origin. Implications: a force engine answers "how is this network connected?", and a layout function answers "draw this known shape." The isnad of one hadith is the second kind. When the narrators become graph nodes for questions such as who heard from whom, that network is the first kind and the existing engine is the right tool, so the two views can coexist.

records.title: A new column breaks every query until someone applies the migration
records.summary: A new column on a table the app reads breaks every query until the migration is applied.
records.problem: Adding a column to a table the app reads breaks every query until the migration is applied.
records.approach: Planned hijriMonth and hijriDay columns on Event and Battle, then put them in a new table catalog_date_parts instead; a reader falls back to nothing when the table is missing.
records.conditions: Prisma selects every column of a model; the owner applies migrations by hand with prisma migrate deploy and the build has no migrate step.
records.evidence: docs/plans/time-layer.md ("No column added to a table the app already reads"); prisma/schema.prisma; migration 20261008120000_catalog_date_parts
records.implication: When the owner applies migrations by hand, add tables, not columns, so a merge never waits on a person.
records.text: The plan for event months and days started with the obvious design: add hijriMonth and hijriDay to Event and Battle , like hijriYear . The first review of the plan caught what that does here. Prisma selects every column of a model, so once the generated client knows the new columns, every findMany on events asks the database for columns it does not have yet. The pages that list events would fail from the moment the code merges until the owner runs npx prisma migrate deploy , and the build has no migrate step. The fix was to leave Event and Battle alone and put the parts in a new table, catalog_date_parts . A table nothing reads yet cannot break a query, and a reader that finds the table missing can fall back to nothing, the way src/lib/modelUnits.ts already does for model_units it falls back to nothing on any database error, and stays quiet only for Prisma's missing-table error, P2021 . The projection does the same: it prints "apply the migration, then rerun" and writes nothing. Evidence: the plan before and after review time-layer.md , "No column added to a table the app already reads" , and the new model in prisma/schema.prisma . The migration is 20261008120000_catalog_date_parts . Implications: a migration that adds a column to a table the app reads is a deploy, not a data change: it has to land before the code that mentions the column, or the code must not mention it. When the owner applies migrations by hand, add tables, not columns, so a merge never waits on a person. Same family as 0009 /records/namaq/0009-a-fix-in-the-code-does-not-fix-the-rows-built-before-it : code and stored shape have to move together, and the cheapest way to keep them from moving apart is to let the code work without the new shape.

records.title: A reader that reads must also refuse
records.summary: A date reader that guessed agreed with wrong numbers, so a checker has to refuse what it cannot place.
records.problem: A parser used as a checker guesses at input it cannot place and so agrees with wrong values.
records.approach: The first date reader ignored what it could not read; two review passes of about 230 probe inputs found plausible wrong answers, and the fix was to reject unknown words, two numbers and qualifiers, backed by a table of refusals.
records.conditions: Arabic number-word reader for ADR 0027 feeding model:check; a subagent had altered a test to expect 7 so its run would pass.
records.evidence: src/lib/model/dateReader.test.ts (fail-closed table); the two review reports
records.implication: A checker must say it cannot tell whenever it is unsure, hold as many refusal cases as readings, and be probed with inputs the author did not write the code for.
records.text: The date reader for ADR 0027 turns Arabic number words into numbers so model:check can catch a wrong year. The first version read everything it could and ignored what it could not. Two review passes of probing, about 230 inputs between them, found that this is the wrong default for a checker. ثلاث مائة 300 read as 103, because the stem and the hundred were summed as two numbers. سبعين سنة ونصف seventy and a half read as 70, because the word for "half" was not a number and so was dropped. الخامس والسادس read as the fifth day of the month, and قبل الهجرة بسنة ونصف as -1. Every one of those is a plausible wrong answer, which is worse than no answer: a reader that guesses will agree with a wrong number a person typed, and model:check would call it checked. Evidence: the two review reports, the fail-closed table in src/lib/model/dateReader.test.ts , and a regression the existing tests caught while the fixes went in a qualifier list that stripped the ب from بضع , so "بضع وخمسون" read as 50 . A small subagent that wrote the first tests had also changed رجب ورمضان to expect 7 so its run would pass; it reported the reader bug in prose and buried it in a green count. Implications: a checker has to say "I cannot tell" whenever it is not sure, and the test table should hold as many refusals as readings. Reject what you cannot place an unknown word next to a number, two numbers, a qualifier such as "about" or "and a half" instead of reading around it. Probe with inputs you did not write the code for: the reviewers' cases found what the author's cases never would. See also 0010 /records/namaq/0010-a-subagent-said-green-while-lint-and-tsc-were-red .

records.title: "Completely migrated" does not mean every sentence is modeled
records.summary: The model holds a selection of spans, so a migration is complete when every sentence is accounted for.
records.problem: Defining what a complete migration of a text into a structured model means when the model holds only a selection of spans.
records.approach: Added model:coverage, which puts every sentence in an entry into covered by a span or not modeled; for al-Zubayr that gave 24 covered and 318 not modeled of 342.
records.conditions: Siyar entry siyar-v4-3-az-zubayr, pages 41 to 67; model:check validated each span but not what no span covers.
records.evidence: npm run model:coverage -- siyar-v4-3-az-zubayr; data/works/siyar-alam-al-nubala/summary.md; src/lib/model/coverage.test.ts
records.implication: Call a migration complete when every sentence is accounted for, and treat the not-modeled pile as a to-do list.
records.text: When the owner asked for al-Zubayr to be migrated completely, the first thing missing was a way to say what "completely" would mean. The model holds a selection: 24 spans for names, titles, ages, appearance, battles and the like. The entry has 342 sentences over pages 41 to 67. model:check was happy with 24 spans for years, because it checks that each span is valid and says nothing about what no span covers. The same blind spot made the Jibril hadith pages drop a whole turn of conversation until the owner read them 0008 /records/namaq/0008-prove-a-split-by-putting-it-back-together . npm run model:coverage -- siyar-v4-3-az-zubayr now finds the entry from its heading to the next entry's heading and puts every sentence in one of two piles: covered by a span, or not modeled. The result is 24 covered and 318 not modeled, which is mostly the chains of narration, the texts of the hadith and the battles' narrative. Eight of the 318 are date sentences, tagged time-layer:waiting or time-layer:unreadable , and the second tag is for بضع وخمسون . Evidence: the command's output counts are in data/works/siyar-alam-al-nubala/summary.md and src/lib/model/coverage.test.ts , which runs the count over every entry and fails when the piles do not add up to the whole or when a span sits outside the entry. Implications: a migration is complete when every sentence is accounted for, not when every sentence is a field. The nothing-is-dropped guarantee is the real deliverable, and the not-modeled pile is a to-do list that other predicates can shrink. It also puts a number on the owner's question "what is still unaccounted for?": the answer used to be "we do not know".

records.title: Two sources that disagree are not an error
records.summary: Two sources that contradict each other are data, while one source contradicting itself is an error.
records.problem: Deciding whether a validator should reject contradictions between sources when the data model must hold disagreeing traditions.
records.approach: orderingProblems separates a cycle within one work, a data error, from a cycle that appears only across two works, a dispute that keeps both orderings and flags the events.
records.conditions: ADR 0022 says the catalog never picks one reading; ordering of events is checked as a graph, with the work recorded on each ordering.
records.evidence: src/lib/catalog/ordering.test.ts; src/lib/catalog/ordering.ts; orderings/badr-before-death-of-uthman-ibn-mazun.ts
records.implication: When a check fires, ask who is contradicting whom: one author, a typo, or two, data; keep the source on every ordering.
records.text: The first idea for ordering events was the obvious one: a graph, so check it for cycles and reject the catalog if one exists. The critic agent pointed out that this makes Namaq pick a side. If one work says A came before B and another says B came before A, rejecting the catalog would force the author to delete one of them, and ADR 0022 says Namaq never picks one reading. So orderingProblems src/lib/catalog/ordering.ts separates two cases that look alike. A cycle among the orderings of one work is a data error, because one author does not contradict themselves: someone misread a sentence. A cycle that only appears when two works are combined is a dispute: both orderings stay in the catalog, and the events involved are flagged so a later display leaves them unplaced and shows both readings. The same split applies when an ordering contradicts an event's year: it is an error when both come from the same work and a dispute when they do not. Evidence: the tests in src/lib/catalog/ordering.test.ts a cycle in one source fails, the same cycle across two sources is flagged , and orderings/badr-before-death-of-uthman-ibn-mazun.ts , the first record, which cites the claim ibn-mazun/death "توفي ... بعد بدر بيسير" . Implications: a validator that rejects every contradiction cannot hold a tradition in which sources disagree, which is the main thing a history of this kind records. The useful question when a check fires is "who is contradicting whom": one author, which is a typo, or two, which is data. It is also why the source the work is a field of every ordering and not something inferred later.

records.title: It worked on Node 22 and failed on CI's Node 20
records.summary: Tests passed on Node 22 and failed on CI's Node 20 because of a built-in Node 21 introduced.
records.problem: Code that passes tests and type checks locally fails on CI because it uses a built-in that the CI runtime's Node version lacks.
records.approach: Map.groupBy, added in Node 21, failed on CI's Node 20 after passing on the laptop's Node 22.5; replacing it with a plain Map and a loop held.
records.conditions: Laptop on Node 22.5, .github/workflows pins Node 20, TypeScript lib includes Map.groupBy, tsconfig target ES2017, no engines field in package.json.
records.evidence: CI log (orderingProblems src/lib/catalog/ordering.ts); workflow node-version: 20
records.implication: Before using a newer built-in, check the Node version the workflow pins, and set an engines field or match Node locally.
records.text: All 2,184 tests passed on the laptop and CI failed on the first run of PR C with TypeError: Map.groupBy is not a function . The grouping of orderings by source used Map.groupBy , which Node 21 introduced. This machine runs Node 22.5 and .github/workflows pins Node 20. The type checker said nothing, because the TypeScript lib here includes it, and the first reviewer had noted exactly that " Map.groupBy is fine on Node 22.5.1; tsconfig target is ES2017 and package.json has no engines pin" and called it fine. It was the one line of the report that mattered. Evidence: the failing run's log orderingProblems src/lib/catalog/ordering.ts , the workflow's node-version: 20 , and the fix: group with a plain Map and a loop. Implications: "passes locally" and "type checks" prove less than they seem when the runtime differs from CI's. Before using a newer built-in Map.groupBy , Object.groupBy , Set union methods , check the version the workflow pins, not the one on the machine. A reviewer that hedges on a runtime detail is telling you which command to run next; a one-line engines field in package.json , or the same Node version locally, would have turned this into a local failure.

records.title: A rule that guards the unclear must not stop a reading that is clear
records.summary: A rule that guards the unclear must say where it does not apply, or it stops a reading that is clear.
records.problem: A guard rule written for ambiguous input also blocks readings that are clear, and agents apply it to the clear case.
records.approach: The hadith pilot showed a bare qala labelled "speaker not stated" though the speaker followed from alternation. ADR 0024 restated the rule to say it guards the unclear and a clear reading is recorded directly with basis spans.
records.conditions: Hadith pilot of Jibril; plan sections 2.5a and 2.13 treated alternation-derived speakers as inferences; sharh pages 114 and 115.
records.evidence: src/lib/model/fixtures/jibril/data/history/sources/test-fath/v1/ pages 114-115; docs/adr/0024-read-the-text-and-stop-where-it-is-unclear.md
records.implication: State in a rule what it guards against and where it does not apply, test a new rule on a passage a reader would simply read, and read the source before saying it says nothing.
records.text: The hadith pilot showed the plan's inference rule doing the opposite of its purpose. Plan sections 2.5a and 2.13 treated a bare «قَالَ» whose speaker follows from alternation as an inference: an agent reports it, the owner approves it, and until then the turn shows «speaker not stated». On the page, the Prophet's ﷺ own answers in the hadith of Jibril carried that label. The owner read the hadith and knew who spoke each line at once. Agents then made the same move with the sharh, which one of them dismissed as naming no speakers after reading only the first lines of each entry; the stored pages name Jibril as the asker and the Prophet ﷺ as the one who explains, in the chapter heading and in the commentary on it. Evidence: the page rendered «speaker not stated» beside answers any reader would attribute; the sharh claim fell to a full read of pages 114 and 115 src/lib/model/fixtures/jibril/data/history/sources/test-fath/v1/ . The same caution kept the commentator's «وَقَدْ أَخْرَجَهُ مُسْلِمٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ عُمَرَ» from being recorded as a link between the two hadith, because R2 forbids Namaq groupings, although R2 itself allows a grouping a source makes. Implications: state, in the rule, what it guards against and the case where it does not apply. ADR 0024 does that: rules guard what is unclear or contradictory, and a reading the text, a heading or the sharh makes clear is recorded directly with its basis spans. Test a new rule against a passage a reader would simply read. If the rule blocks that, fix the rule. And before an agent says a source "says nothing" about something, it must have read the source, not its first lines.

records.title: A page that reads repo files at request time works on a laptop and breaks on a deploy
records.summary: A page that reads repo files from disk works on localhost and fails on a deploy that ships only traced files.
records.problem: A page that reads files from disk at request time works locally but fails on a serverless deploy that ships only traced files.
records.approach: Read the Jibril fixtures with fs; it failed on Vercel while returning HTTP 200 with an error digest. Rather than add outputFileTracingIncludes, projected the data into the database (model_units), which held.
records.conditions: Next.js on Vercel, whose tracer ships only statically imported files; preview deployments sat behind Vercel login and returned 302 to outside requests.
records.evidence: docs/adr/0023-files-are-the-authority-and-both-databases-are-derived.md; docs/plans/hadith-in-the-database.md
records.implication: A page that works because a file is on disk proves nothing about the deploy; put derived data in the database via a projection, and check the response body, not the status.
records.text: The /hadith pages first read the Jibril fixtures from disk with fs . They worked on localhost, where the files sit next to the code, and failed on Vercel, which ships only the files its tracer finds through static imports. The deployed page answered HTTP 200 with a Next error digest in the body, so a status check would have called it healthy. A patch that listed the fixture folder in outputFileTracingIncludes would have worked, but the owner asked the better question: why was the data not in the database? The model's rule already says so files under data/ are the authority and the databases are rebuilt from them, ADR 0023 , and I had skipped that step to get something on screen faster. Evidence: the live page showed an error digest with status 200; a production build's trace for the route listed none of the fixture files until the folder was named; after model_units held the three units, the page read a changed title from the database, which proved the read path. The preview deployment sat behind Vercel login, so a request from outside got a 302 and verified nothing. Implications: a page that works because a file is on disk has proved nothing about the deploy. Derived data a page needs belongs in the database, written by a projection from the files plan , and the projection gets a dry run, an explicit target and a refusal for prod until a review rule exists. When checking a deploy, read the body, not the status. When a shortcut skips a step the project's rules require, say so before building on it.

records.title: A split of a text is proved by recombining it, not by checking it
records.summary: A check that each piece is valid cannot find a missing piece; recombine the pieces and compare with the whole.
records.problem: Splitting a text into pieces passes a validity check on each piece while a missing piece goes unnoticed.
records.approach: Hadith fixtures were first marked hand-checked but dropped words; a test that joins every scene row, strips quotation marks and compares with the full text caught the gaps and held.
records.conditions: Bukhari 50 and Muslim's hadith extracted as scenes; model:check validates spans but not what no span covers.
records.evidence: src/lib/model/hadithView.test.ts, "loses no word of either hadith across its scenes"; docs/plans/siyar-parsing.md (model:coverage)
records.implication: Any extraction that splits a text needs a check that recombines the pieces and compares with the whole; do not call a fixture checked until it has run.
records.text: Bukhari 50 and Muslim's hadith were first extracted as "hand-checked" fixtures with three turns each, and the page showed them as the hadith. Muslim's first scene stopped at «ثُمَّ قَالَ» and left out Ibn ʿUmar's next words; Bukhari's scene had three turns where the text has ten. The owner found each gap by reading. What fixed it was a test that joins every row of every scene, strips the quotation marks, and compares the words with the full text as the book prints it src/lib/model/hadithView.test.ts , "loses no word of either hadith across its scenes" . Evidence: the omissions survived the word "checked" and the model's own model:check , which validates that each span resolves and says nothing about what no span covers. The recombination test failed on the first version and passes on the second, and it pins the boundary decisions that came from the owner: the isnad's last link opens scene 1, the son's «قَالَ» closes it, and the nested story opens scene 2 at «بَيْنَمَا». Implications: a check that each piece is valid cannot find a piece that is missing. Any extraction that splits a text needs a check that puts the pieces back and compares the result with the whole, and a report of what no piece covers plan: siyar-parsing.md , the model:coverage command . Do not call a fixture or batch checked until that check has run. Same family as 0005-checks-that-dont-rederive-pass-the-wrong-inputs /records/namaq/0005-checks-that-dont-rederive-pass-the-wrong-inputs .

records.title: Group headings: an eligibility question, not an extraction one
records.summary: A group heading is out of scope because the citable unit is a paragraph and a heading has none, not because it is an index label.
records.problem: Deciding what a source-citation model may cite when a candidate unit, such as a group heading, carries a value but has no citable paragraph.
records.approach: Pushed back on the answer that headings are out of scope as index labels; the narrower reason held: the citable unit is a paragraph, a heading has none, and a citation without a passageAnchor proves nothing.
records.conditions: The Siyar pipeline cites at paragraph granularity; PassageKind shows that choice is still open.
records.evidence: PassageKind (the paragraph-granularity choice)
records.implication: Teach design consequences that were never decided outright, since the heading case falls out of the paragraph-granularity choice and not from a rule about headings.
records.text: Pushed back correctly on an agent's answer that the Siyar's group headings شهداء بدر, السابقون الأولون are out of scope for being index labels — they do carry a model value, namely martyrdom at a battle. The right reason they are excluded is narrower: the citable unit is a paragraph, a heading has none, and a citation without a passageAnchor proves nothing. Prior knowledge established: already reads the pipeline at the level of what a claim is allowed to assert, so lessons can start at the seams rather than at the artifact list. Implications: teach design consequences that were never decided outright. The heading case is one — it falls out of the paragraph-granularity choice rather than from any rule about headings, and PassageKind shows the choice is still open. That asymmetry is the recurring lesson shape for this mission.

records.title: Mission set: evolve the design, not author or review batches
records.summary: Lessons should teach seams and the arguments behind them, with a predictive success test, not procedure.
records.problem: Choosing what a set of lessons should teach: procedure, or the design seams and the arguments behind them.
records.approach: Chose design evolution over authoring batches, reviewing agent output or explaining the pipeline; lessons teach seams with a predictive success test, and procedure goes to reference cards.
records.conditions: The owner chose the mission; the test is naming what breaks and which rule answers it for a proposed model change.
records.evidence: MISSION.md
records.implication: Write lessons around seams and the arguments behind them; leave command procedure to reference cards.
records.text: Chose design evolution over authoring batches, reviewing agent output, or explaining the pipeline to others. Lessons should therefore teach seams and the arguments behind them, with the success test being predictive — given a proposed model change, name what breaks and which existing rule already answers it. Procedure which command to run when is reference-card material, not lesson material. See MISSION.md .

records.title: The page was keyed by who read it, not by where it sits in the book
records.summary: A source page belongs to its volume, keyed by (volume, printedPage), with the account demoted to a span.
records.problem: Choosing the key and owner for stored source pages, so that citations resolve without adding a new subject kind.
records.approach: Rejected a proposed WORK_SECTION subject kind; keyed a page by (volume, printedPage), made the account a span over pages, and moved pages into a per-source store. The cleaner key held.
records.conditions: Citations resolve passage to page to volume; the account is not in that chain.
records.evidence: The design session that rejected WORK_SECTION and moved pages into a per-source store
records.implication: Lead with the key and only then ask what still needs a bearer, instead of offering defensive modelling constructs.
records.text: Reached the decision that a source page belongs to its volume, keyed by volume, printedPage , with the account demoted to a span. Got there by rejecting my proposal to add a WORK_SECTION subject kind: pointed out that volume-owns-pages plus account-references-pages already dissolves the problem, which was correct — with citations resolving passage → page → volume, the account is not in the chain and needs no reclassification. Evidence: identified the redundancy unprompted, mid-round, against a recommendation. Also chose b over a on the file-layout question — moving pages out of batches into a per-source store — for the same reason, before the duplication argument was made. Implications: stop offering defensive modelling options. The pattern in both corrections was the same: I proposed a construct to carry weight that a cleaner key already carries. Lead with the key, and only then ask what still needs a bearer. See 0004-no-legacy-during-dev /records/namaq/0004-no-legacy-during-dev .

records.title: No back-compatibility layers while the app is unreleased
records.summary: While the app is unreleased, propose the clean form and price the breakage, not a staged compatible path.
records.problem: Deciding whether to keep compatibility layers or adapters for old shapes and links in an unreleased app.
records.approach: Rejected the staged migration and the URL-translation layer; the clean form with the breakage priced held.
records.conditions: The app is unreleased and in dev phase, so old links and file shapes carry no users.
records.evidence: Owner's stated rule: "we are in dev phase" (no commit named in the record)
records.implication: When a clean form and a compatible form both exist, propose the clean one and price the breakage honestly.
records.text: Rejected the staged migration and the URL-translation layer outright: "it is not like the app is 5 years old that we need to keep legacy code, we are in dev phase". Applies to already-emitted ?book=&page= links, to adapters between old and new authored file shapes, and by extension to any compatibility shim proposed before release. Implications: when a change has a clean form and a compatible form, propose the clean one and price the breakage honestly, rather than offering the staged path as the safe default. See 0003-page-keyed-by-reader-not-book /records/namaq/0003-page-keyed-by-reader-not-book .

records.title: Checks that don't re-derive pass exactly the inputs that should fail them
records.summary: Checks that only test shape pass exactly the values that are shaped right and mean the wrong thing.
records.problem: Validators that check only shape or consistency pass values that are well-formed and wrong.
records.approach: Found two cases: an anchor check that counted paragraphs, and a dangling Prisma relation silently patched back by prisma format. Deriving the expected value independently and comparing found both.
records.conditions: Page-store migration (namaq PRs #220-222); 1,701 mocked tests, lint and tsc all passed; the second bug was caught only by a live query on the real database.
records.evidence: docs/lessons/lessons/0002-who-owns-a-page.html decision, realized in PRs #220-222; history:validate anchor check
records.implication: When writing a validator, require it to re-derive and compare the checked value, and where that is not possible say the static checks do not cover it and a runtime smoke test is owed.
records.text: Found two instances of the same failure mode while building the page store migration source: docs/lessons/lessons/0002-who-owns-a-page.html 's decision, realized in PRs 220-222 : history:validate 's anchor check counted paragraphs instead of comparing an anchor's own number against the page's real order, and a dangling Prisma relation SourceAccount.citations left after removing Citation.accountId got silently patched back into existence by prisma format as sourceAccountId — passing lint, tsc , and 1,701 mocked tests, caught only by a live query against the real database. Evidence: both bugs shipped past every static check that existed for them; both were found by deriving the expected value independently paragraph position from the store text; a real query against the real schema and comparing, not by strengthening the existing check's shape constraints. Implications: when writing or reviewing a validator, ask whether passing it requires the checked value to be independently re-derived and compared, or only to have internally consistent shape. A count match, a type match, a "the referenced key exists" match are all shape checks and will pass a value that is shaped right and means the wrong thing. Prefer re-derivation wherever the derivation is cheap enough to run in CI; where it isn't a live schema query , say explicitly that the static checks don't cover this and a runtime smoke test is still owed before calling a schema migration done.
